stale-projects.dependencies.name: Packages of old projects
stale-projects.dependencies.line: Packages of projects you have not touched
stale-projects.dependencies.what: The packages in the node_modules folders of Node.js projects you have not changed for a long time.
stale-projects.dependencies.made-by: Your package manager, such as npm or Yarn, when it installed the project's packages.
stale-projects.dependencies.if-removed: Your code stays; installing the project's packages again brings them back.
stale-projects.dependencies.comes-back: Only when you install the project's packages again.
stale-projects.build-output.name: Builds of old projects
stale-projects.build-output.line: Built files of projects you have not touched
stale-projects.build-output.what: What a project's build tool made and can make again, such as its target or build folder, in projects you have not changed for a long time.
stale-projects.build-output.made-by: The project's build tool, when you built it.
stale-projects.build-output.if-removed: Your code stays; the next build makes them again, which takes a while.
stale-projects.python-environments.name: Old Python environments
stale-projects.python-environments.line: Python setups of projects you have not touched
stale-projects.python-environments.what: A Python project's own copy of Python and its packages (.venv or venv), in projects you have not changed for a long time.
stale-projects.python-environments.made-: You or your Python tools, when you set the project up.
stale-projects.python-environments.if-re: Your code stays; to work on the project again, make a new environment and install its packages, and find again any package you added by hand.
stale-projects.python-environments.comes: Only when you make the environment again.
stale-projects.rust-build-cache.name: Rust build cache
stale-projects.rust-build-cache.line: Build files of Rust projects you have not touched
stale-projects.rust-build-cache.what: Files Cargo keeps only to build Rust projects faster, often gigabytes, even in a project you work on every day.
stale-projects.rust-build-cache.made-by: Cargo and the Rust compiler; cargo llvm-cov, when it measured test coverage.
stale-projects.rust-build-cache.if-remov: Your code and your built programs stay; the next build takes longer once.
stale-projects.enabled.label: Old projects
stale-projects.enabled.description: Finds the installed packages and build output of projects you have not changed for a long time, and Rust's build cache. Your code is never touched.
stale-projects.unused-for-days.label: Offer projects unchanged for
stale-projects.unused-for-days.descripti: A project's packages and build output are offered only once nothing in it has changed for this many days, at least 30. Rust's build cache is offered after 7 days without a build, whatever this says.
stale-projects.title: {project} · {folder}
stale-projects.reason.dependencies: Nothing in this project has changed since {date}. Running {command} in it downloads these packages again.
stale-projects.reason.build-output: Nothing in this project has changed since {date}. Running {command} in it builds this again, which takes a while.
stale-projects.reason.python-environment: Nothing in this project has changed since {date}. {command} and an install of the project's packages make it again; packages you added by hand and listed nowhere are lost.
stale-projects.reason.rust-build-cache: Only Cargo reads this, to build faster, and no build has used it for {days} days. The next {command} makes what it needs again.
stale-projects.left-out.unread: Fresher could not read every folder of this project, so it cannot tell when it last changed. It is kept.
stale-projects.left-out.recent: It or its project changed within the days set in Settings, so it is kept. A scan after those days offers it.
stale-projects.left-out.cache-recent: A build used it within the last 7 days, so it is kept.
